claim: The frozen Step7H warning rule is non-trivial: it does not reduce to always alerting or never alerting.
basis: Across all frozen operating points, Step7H sensitivity is >0 and false-alert rate is <1, while ALWAYS-RED has sensitivity=1/FAR=1 and ALWAYS-GREEN has sensitivity=0/FAR=0.

claim: Relative to ALWAYS-RED, Step7H sacrifices some crossing sensitivity but removes a large fraction of false alerts.
basis: Step7H alert sensitivity is roughly 0.77–0.87 while false-alert rates are roughly 0.31–0.37 instead of 1.0.

claim: Step7H alert precision is materially higher than the prevalence-level precision of an ALWAYS-RED rule.
basis: ALWAYS-RED precision equals crossing prevalence, whereas Step7H selectively alerts and achieves higher precision at every frozen group.

claim: The RED channel is selective for urgent crossings: false-RED rates among non-urgent instances remain very low while urgent RED precision is substantially above the ALWAYS-RED urgent-prevalence baseline.
basis: Step7H false-RED rates are below 1% across the reported groups, while urgent RED precision is roughly 0.44–0.89.

claim: Step7H provides a useful sensitivity–false-alert trade-off in the virtual-geofence simulation.
basis: It lies between ALWAYS-RED and ALWAYS-GREEN on the expected trade-off curve, but this remains a simulation/decision-layer result.

claim: Step7H achieves near-perfect crossing detection without substantial false alerts.
basis: Alert sensitivity is below 0.9 and false-alert rates remain around 0.31–0.37 at the frozen operating points.

claim: The trivial-baseline comparison establishes real-world warning effectiveness.
basis: The experiment uses a normalized virtual geofence and simulated response thresholds rather than field deployment.

claim: Step7H remains the primary operational warning protocol; Step18 should be reported as secondary/ablation evidence.
basis: This hierarchy was already frozen in the revision protocol and R5A audit.
